candidates.computation_change_reason: The column taxonomy distinguishes use-based limits (Domestic, Irrigation, Livestock or Wildlife), aquatic toxicity limits (Acute, Chronic), human-health limits, concentration limits (Daily Max Conc, Monthly Avg Conc, Daily Max Total, Monthly Avg Total), and load limits (Daily Max Load, Daily Avg Load) with different units (ug/l vs lb/day). Different readings of which column governs a given discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period would change the selected enforceable numeric limit (A), which monitoring forms are required to support compliance demonstration (B), and whether absent or non-numeric results are subject to numeric comparison or treated as non-enforceable/no-data (C).

This heading bounds the pollutant subset for which the following rows supply limit values. Whether it is read as an exhaustive list of pesticide/PCB parameters covered on this page, or as a categorical label only, affects which parameters are in scope for limit lookup (A), which pesticide/PCB monitoring obligations are anchored to this table (B), and how missing results for related analytes are classified when not listed here (C).

Numeric limits appear only under Human Health and downstream concentration/load columns while aquatic and use-based columns are N/A. Interpreting whether the human-health daily max (0.05408611 ug/l), monthly average (0.036057407 ug/l), concentration-total, or load limits apply—and whether aquatic N/A means no aquatic limit or limit not shown—would change the enforceable limit selected for comparison (A), the monitoring basis required for that parameter (B), and whether a missing Aldrin result is an unresolved compliance gap or a non-comparable case (C).

Both a Chronic Aquatic limit (0.18368676) and separate Human Health concentration/load limits are populated. Choosing chronic aquatic versus human-health daily max, monthly average, or load limits as the governing standard would materially change exceedance determination (A), the monitoring and reporting needed to demonstrate compliance (B), and how to treat absent Chlordane results when the applicable limit type is uncertain (C).

Acute Aquatic (0.73), Chronic Aquatic (0.00854357), and Human Health concentration/load limits coexist and differ by orders of magnitude. Which limit category and statistic (daily max vs monthly average vs load) is operative would directly change compliance outcomes (A), the monitoring design implied for toxaphene (B), and whether a missing result leaves compliance unresolved or reflects a non-applicable comparison basis (C).
